bug_semantics: free5GC NEF (github.com/free5gc/nef, tracked as submodule NFs/nef) mounts the nnef-oam SBI route group with no inbound OAuth2/bearer middleware. A network attacker who can reach NEF on the SBI can GET /nnef-oam/v1/ with no Authorization header; gin dispatches to GetOamIndex, which returns HTTP 200 OK with a null body. At the GHSA-validated revision (nef 5ce35eab / free5gc v4.2.1) NewServer() does group := router.Group(factory.NefOamResUriPrefix); applyRoutes(group, getOamRoutes()) with no Group.Use(auth). The current handler is a stub, but the defect is group-scoped: every route on nnef-oam inherits the missing auth boundary. CWE-306/CWE-862. Same missing-inbound-auth pattern as NEF traffic-influence and PFD-management.
flaw_origin: The exploitable OAM handler was first written in nef commit 84a33e9458e9209c5c379af05d4834c151b2e2d1 (2021-11-18, 'Add oam service' by free5gc-org): it registered GET / on getOamEndpoints, added Processor.GetOamIndex returning http.StatusOK, and advertised nnef-oam in serviceList, all without any token check. Immediate parent 4bc48a893a7f7dff47be51ddec4efcf5faf52b4b still had getOamEndpoints() []Endpoint{} and no oam_handler.go, so no-token GET could not reach a 200 handler. An empty unauthenticated /nnef-oam/v1 group had existed since 3ae828b1315fde7e0d9da74ae25b23816aad4a08 (2020-10-28, Tim Liu, 'New and run SBI server'); that placeholder is not this CVE's BIC because it had no OAM handler. Later path/name refactors (0bcbd0d rename, b0a2d43 getOamRoutes, cc71387 c.JSON(StatusOK,nil)) and free5gc submodule add 3022243 are moves/gitlinks, not first-writes. Outbound NRF OAuth (nef PRs #2/#4, 2024) never added inbound middleware, so the 2021 unauthenticated handler remained the live sink until 2026.

The live sink at the advisory revision is an unauthenticated gin group at /nnef-oam/v1 plus GetOamIndex returning 200 OK, reproduced without a bearer token while outbound OAuth was enabled. Code lives in submodule github.com/free5gc/nef; free5gc/free5gc only stores the gitlink. BIC search used first-party paths (server.go OAM mount, api_oam.go GET /, processor/oam.go StatusOK), then git log -S GetOamIndex and git log -L on getOamRoutes, not an AI-marker hunt. Its parent 4bc48a89 is present and was tree-checked: the handler file and GetOamIndex symbol are absent and getOamEndpoints is still empty, so the PoC 200 path did not exist yet. The earlier 3ae828b empty-group mount is a related missing-middleware placeholder but not this CVE's first-write of the reachable handler; subsequent renames/refactors and the 2024 free5gc submodule add are not BICs.
